text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Five cabinet ministers convened an emergency meeting in Harare on Wednesday to discuss a probe into allegations that senior ruling ZANU PF party and goverment officials siphoned millions of dollars from the "war of liberation compensation fund", sources said.

- Master of Zimbabwe's High Court, Jacob Moyo, suspended from his post in January, has been accused of corruption and abuse of power, including allegations that he extorted money from members of the public.

- State airliner Air Zimbabwe is losing Z$24 million annually by maintaining a highly expensive contract with Catercraft (Pvt) Ltd, a Harare-based catering firm with close ties to the ruling ZANU PF party, industry sources said.
- The state Posts and Telecommunications Corp has prepared a comprehensive plan for its privatisation by the year 2000.
- Three black Zimbabwean business partners have acquired a 52 percent local interest in Richard Ellis Africa, one of the leading real estate consultants and valuers in the country.

- The Zimbabwe government wants the state-owned Cold Storage Co to retain its monopoly of beef exports and the Grain Marketing Board to retain sole management of the strategic grain reserves, Agriculture Minister Dennis Norman said.
- Cheaper electricity could soon be generated at Lake Kariba as its water level continues to rise.
